## Continuation Wave 22 — Plan 11 — Tool Libraries, Salvage, and Repair Apprenticeships

Wave 22 adds a new owner-bound layer for **tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners**. Material anchors include **a spokeshave with a black grip, a tray of tin pins, a brace joined with jute, and a checkout card marked with a circle**. Observable markers include **grip shadow, pin count, jute brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return map**.

### Pass 232 — Black Grip Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners; it does not mint a second tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships ledger. Treat the visible markers grip shadow, pin count, jute brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return map as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Black Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees grip shadow, pin count, jute brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return map with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Black Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a spokeshave with a black grip, a tray of tin pins, a brace joined with jute, and a checkout card marked with a circle become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Black Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Black Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present grip shadow, pin count, jute brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return map with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Black Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a spokeshave with a black grip, a tray of tin pins, a brace joined with jute, and a checkout card marked with a circle as physical evidence and grip shadow, pin count, jute brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return map as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Black Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Black Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Black Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises grip shadow, pin count, jute brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return map at their boundary values.

**Black Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Black Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 24 — Plan 11 — Tool Libraries, Salvage, and Repair Apprenticeships

Wave 24 adds a new owner-bound layer for **tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners**. Material anchors include **a file with a turquoise grip, a tray of lead pins, a brace joined with cotton, and a checkout card marked in a corner square**. Observable markers include **grip tint, pin count, cotton brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return atlas**.

### Pass 254 — Turquoise Grip Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners; it does not mint a second tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships ledger. Treat the visible markers grip tint, pin count, cotton brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return atlas as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Turquoise Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees grip tint, pin count, cotton brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return atlas with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Turquoise Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a file with a turquoise grip, a tray of lead pins, a brace joined with cotton, and a checkout card marked in a corner square become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Turquoise Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Turquoise Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Turquoise Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 25 — Plan 11 — Tool Libraries, Salvage, and Repair Apprenticeships

Wave 25 adds a new owner-bound layer for **tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners**. Material anchors include **a bradawl with an orange grip, a tray of brass pins, a brace joined with hemp, and a checkout card marked with a slash**. Observable markers include **grip heat, pin count, hemp brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return compass**.

### Pass 265 — Orange Grip Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners; it does not mint a second tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships ledger. Treat the visible markers grip heat, pin count, hemp brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return compass as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Orange Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees grip heat, pin count, hemp brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return compass with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Orange Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a bradawl with an orange grip, a tray of brass pins, a brace joined with hemp, and a checkout card marked with a slash become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Orange Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Orange Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present grip heat, pin count, hemp brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return compass with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Orange Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a bradawl with an orange grip, a tray of brass pins, a brace joined with hemp, and a checkout card marked with a slash as physical evidence and grip heat, pin count, hemp brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return compass as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Orange Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Orange Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Orange Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises grip heat, pin count, hemp brace load, queue debt, learner confidence, and return compass at their boundary values.

**Orange Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Orange Grip Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 27 — Plan 11 — Tool Libraries, Salvage, and Repair Apprenticeships

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners**. Material anchors include **a rivet gauge with an amber notch, a coil of copper wire, a leather apron with three cuts, and a locker tag etched with a wave**. Observable markers include **gauge alignment, wire temper, apron wear, locker drift, queue pressure, and handoff route**.

### Pass 287 — Amber Gauge Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners; it does not mint a second tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships ledger. Treat the visible markers gauge alignment, wire temper, apron wear, locker drift, queue pressure, and handoff route as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Amber Gauge Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees gauge alignment, wire temper, apron wear, locker drift, queue pressure, and handoff route with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Amber Gauge Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a rivet gauge with an amber notch, a coil of copper wire, a leather apron with three cuts, and a locker tag etched with a wave become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Amber Gauge Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Amber Gauge Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present gauge alignment, wire temper, apron wear, locker drift, queue pressure, and handoff route with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Amber Gauge Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a rivet gauge with an amber notch, a coil of copper wire, a leather apron with three cuts, and a locker tag etched with a wave as physical evidence and gauge alignment, wire temper, apron wear, locker drift, queue pressure, and handoff route as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Amber Gauge Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Amber Gauge Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Amber Gauge Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises gauge alignment, wire temper, apron wear, locker drift, queue pressure, and handoff route at their boundary values.

**Amber Gauge Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Amber Gauge Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 28 — Plan 11 — Tool Libraries, Salvage, and Repair Apprenticeships

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners**. Material anchors include **a file with a red handle, a spool of hemp twine, a vise jaw wrapped in cloth, and a tag punched with two holes**. Observable markers include **file bite, twine fray, vise pressure, tag alignment, queue strain, and return route**.

### Pass 298 — Red Handle Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners; it does not mint a second tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships ledger. Treat the visible markers file bite, twine fray, vise pressure, tag alignment, queue strain, and return route as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Red Handle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees file bite, twine fray, vise pressure, tag alignment, queue strain, and return route with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Red Handle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a file with a red handle, a spool of hemp twine, a vise jaw wrapped in cloth, and a tag punched with two holes become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Red Handle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Red Handle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present file bite, twine fray, vise pressure, tag alignment, queue strain, and return route with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Red Handle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a file with a red handle, a spool of hemp twine, a vise jaw wrapped in cloth, and a tag punched with two holes as physical evidence and file bite, twine fray, vise pressure, tag alignment, queue strain, and return route as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Red Handle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Red Handle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Red Handle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises file bite, twine fray, vise pressure, tag alignment, queue strain, and return route at their boundary values.

**Red Handle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Red Handle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 29 — Plan 11 — Tool Libraries, Salvage, and Repair Apprenticeships

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Material anchors include **a brass awl with green thread, a drawer of copper washers, a mallet face darkened by oil, and a slate ticket marked with a crescent**. Observable markers include **awl point, washer count, mallet face, crescent ticket, bench load, and exchange route**.

### Pass 309 — Green Thread Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners; it does not mint a second tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships ledger. Treat the visible markers awl point, washer count, mallet face, crescent ticket, bench load, and exchange route as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Green Thread Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees awl point, washer count, mallet face, crescent ticket, bench load, and exchange route with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Green Thread Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a brass awl with green thread, a drawer of copper washers, a mallet face darkened by oil, and a slate ticket marked with a crescent become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Green Thread Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

## Continuation Wave 30 — Plan 11 — Tool Libraries, Salvage, and Repair Apprenticeships

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners**. Material anchors include **a chisel with a split ferrule, a tin of brass screws, a bench hook carved with a notch, and a loan slip folded into thirds**. Observable markers include **ferrule spread, screw sheen, notch fit, slip fold, backlog heat, and return path**.

### Pass 320 — Split Ferrule Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners; it does not mint a second tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships ledger. Treat the visible markers ferrule spread, screw sheen, notch fit, slip fold, backlog heat, and return path as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Split Ferrule Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees ferrule spread, screw sheen, notch fit, slip fold, backlog heat, and return path with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Split Ferrule Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a chisel with a split ferrule, a tin of brass screws, a bench hook carved with a notch, and a loan slip folded into thirds become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Split Ferrule Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 31 — Plan 11 — Tool Libraries, Salvage, and Repair Apprenticeships

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners**. Material anchors include **a hacksaw with a blue tooth, a stack of lead washers, a clamp padded with felt, and a tag stamped with a square**. Observable markers include **tooth sharpness, washer stack, felt compression, square mark, bench congestion, and handoff lane**.

### Pass 331 — Blue Tooth Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners; it does not mint a second tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships ledger. Treat the visible markers tooth sharpness, washer stack, felt compression, square mark, bench congestion, and handoff lane as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Blue Tooth Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees tooth sharpness, washer stack, felt compression, square mark, bench congestion, and handoff lane with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Blue Tooth Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a hacksaw with a blue tooth, a stack of lead washers, a clamp padded with felt, and a tag stamped with a square become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Blue Tooth Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Blue Tooth Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present tooth sharpness, washer stack, felt compression, square mark, bench congestion, and handoff lane with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Blue Tooth Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a hacksaw with a blue tooth, a stack of lead washers, a clamp padded with felt, and a tag stamped with a square as physical evidence and tooth sharpness, washer stack, felt compression, square mark, bench congestion, and handoff lane as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Blue Tooth Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Blue Tooth Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Blue Tooth Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises tooth sharpness, washer stack, felt compression, square mark, bench congestion, and handoff lane at their boundary values.

**Blue Tooth Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Blue Tooth Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 33 — Plan 11 — Tool Libraries, Salvage, and Repair Apprenticeships

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners**. Material anchors include **a drill bit with a black collar, a tin tray of clips, a clamp handle wrapped in leather, and a return slip marked with a star**. Observable markers include **collar wear, clip count, handle grip, star mark, bench delay, and return lane**.

### Pass 353 — Black Collar Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners; it does not mint a second tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships ledger. Treat the visible markers collar wear, clip count, handle grip, star mark, bench delay, and return lane as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Black Collar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees collar wear, clip count, handle grip, star mark, bench delay, and return lane with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Black Collar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a drill bit with a black collar, a tin tray of clips, a clamp handle wrapped in leather, and a return slip marked with a star become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Black Collar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Black Collar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present collar wear, clip count, handle grip, star mark, bench delay, and return lane with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Black Collar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a drill bit with a black collar, a tin tray of clips, a clamp handle wrapped in leather, and a return slip marked with a star as physical evidence and collar wear, clip count, handle grip, star mark, bench delay, and return lane as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.
