## Continuation Wave 34 — Plan 11 — Tool Libraries, Salvage, and Repair Apprenticeships

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners**. Material anchors include **a rasp with a green heel, a basket of rivets, a clamp foot wrapped in rope, and a checkout tag marked with a crescent**. Observable markers include **heel wear, rivet count, foot grip, crescent mark, bench backlog, and return corridor**.

### Pass 364 — Green Heel Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, and shelter workshop owners; it does not mint a second tool libraries, salvage, and repair apprenticeships ledger. Treat the visible markers heel wear, rivet count, foot grip, crescent mark, bench backlog, and return corridor as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Green Heel Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees heel wear, rivet count, foot grip, crescent mark, bench backlog, and return corridor with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Green Heel Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a rasp with a green heel, a basket of rivets, a clamp foot wrapped in rope, and a checkout tag marked with a crescent become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Green Heel Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Green Heel Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present heel wear, rivet count, foot grip, crescent mark, bench backlog, and return corridor with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Green Heel Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a rasp with a green heel, a basket of rivets, a clamp foot wrapped in rope, and a checkout tag marked with a crescent as physical evidence and heel wear, rivet count, foot grip, crescent mark, bench backlog, and return corridor as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Green Heel Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Green Heel Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Green Heel Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises heel wear, rivet count, foot grip, crescent mark, bench backlog, and return corridor at their boundary values.

**Green Heel Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Green Heel Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 35 integration closeout receipt — Plan 11: Tool Libraries, Salvage, and Repair Apprenticeships

**Closeout status:** documentation-only; READY FOR PREMISE AUDIT. This receipt does not claim implementation.

**Program role:** inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, shelter workshop, and apprenticeship

**Primary owners:** inventory, crafting, condition, work-order, duty, economy, expedition, shelter workshop, and apprenticeship owners

**Required delta:** a tool-library and repair projection over existing inventory, condition, work-order, and duty owners, with no second loan or queue ledger

**First safe slice:** one tool checkout and return with condition evidence, learner acknowledgement, failure recovery, and archive callback

**Evidence anchors:** a condition tag, a repair bench card, a parts tray, and a learner mark

**Observable signals:** condition age, part count, queue debt, learner confidence, reservation status, and return route

### Closeout boundary

The plan closes at the design boundary where one current owner can publish a fact, one consumer can display or consume it, one command can be issued through the owner, and one recovery path can return the player to a known state. The plan does not create a second ledger, registry, cache authority, save store, event bus, or presentation-owned counter. A row remains design-only until a current source search proves its consumer.

### Integration contract

The first receipt must identify the owner, public API, data file, save section or stateless proof, host route, focused tests, and rollback. It must exercise source age, stale input, duplicate delivery, interruption, correction, keyboard/controller parity, empty and error states, and one delayed content callback. The same seed and ordered inputs must reproduce the result across save, reload, host reopen, and duplicate event delivery.

### Content and failure gate

The first content slice uses salvage lessons, apprentice errors, tool disputes, parts shortages, repair milestones, and workshop callbacks. It includes discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, choice, quiet success, costly success, refusal, unresolved outcome, delayed callback, repeat policy, and retirement rule. It must stop safely for duplicate condition state, local loan counters, hidden crafting costs, queue starvation, and stale checkout UI. Prose can describe evidence and uncertainty but cannot create a gameplay fact.

### Handoff

**MUST PRESERVE:** existing authority, engine-free Core, JSON data authority, deterministic ordering, current save ownership, truthful UI, and active path claims.
